content:
ana-finance: Cascade Health submitted a dispute — they say the platform fee for May was billed twice because they were in a cross-region failover and we billed both primary and standby reserved pools. They want one platform line removed.
devon-sales: their AM forwarded a note saying they ran an active DR failover 2026-05-11 03:00-07:00 UTC. They expected standby pools to be excluded from platform fees during failover.
liam-cs: checking infra 1261 026. Logs show two pools attached to their org: cascade-primary (reserved) and cascade-standby (reserved, hot-standby). During failover traffic shifted to standby and primary was quiesced. Both pools remained in reserved state for May billing.
nana-finance: invoice details:
```
INV-2026-599
line 1: reserved_primary_hours 744 => $44,640
line 2: reserved_standby_hours 744 => $44,640
line 3: platform_fee_primary => $11,160
line 4: platform_fee_standby => $11,160
line 5: support_enterprise => $4,000
```
customer asks to remove platform_fee_standby $11,160.
billing-bot: Invoice INV-2026-599 created 2026-05-13T08:12Z. Metering shows both pools billed under reserved_commit_hours=744 each for cust_cascade_012. No recorded exemption or migration tag for cross-region failover.
devon-sales: Cascade says they submitted a migration notice to ops@redwood but we didn't reply. They insist the standby pool should be considered non-billable platform fee during failover.
liam-cs: technical nuance: standby pool was configured as "hot-standby" (reserved) which by contract is treated as active capacity. We bill platform fees per reserved pool. If customer wanted standby excluded they should have used on-demand standby or requested a waiver.
paula-legal: contract review: SOW addendum for HA configs spells out "hot-standby reservations are billable; platform fee applies per reserved pool unless explicitly waived in writing by Redwood." So default is billable.
carmen-fp: still, this is a renewal risk. Recommend settlement path: either pro-rate platform fee for verified failover window (4h) OR grant a one-time concession equal to 10% of standby platform line (~$1,116) to preserve relationship. Approve up to $2,500 for goodwill.
nana-finance: pro-rate math: $11,160 / 744h = $15/hr. Verified failover 4h => $60. Large delta from customer's ask.
devon-sales: customer will reject $60. Ask to propose $1,500 credit in exchange for signing a HA configuration addendum that clarifies billing for standby pools and establishes a 48h pre-notify requirement for planned failovers.
paula-legal: we can approve $1,500 settlement if AM collects written acceptance and we add a clear clause to their account SOW. Document as exception so it doesn't become precedent.
billing-bot: creating credit memo CM-2026-700 (pending) amount $1,500. Ticket #billing-ops-10021. Ledger hold until signed acceptance.
carmen-fp: approved. Finance issue CM-2026-700 for $1,500 pending signature. Require Cascade to sign HA addendum and acknowledge future billing rules.
liam-cs: ops action: add an alert to flag when two reserved pools exist under same org and failover events occur so AMs can review prior to billing. Rule id: alert-standby-2026-05.
nana-finance: I'll update invoice status to "negotiation_pending" and attach the contract snippet. Will send settlement offer once AM confirms.
devon-sales: will send offer and get signature. I'll note we also need a short help doc explaining standby types to customers.
nana-finance: Cascade accepted $1,500 credit and signed the HA addendum. CM-2026-700 applied. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
